GraceUXGuidelines.Rationale: Mark is a document editor with WYSIWYG, source, project, diff, terminal, import/export, update, and extension-host surfaces.

MigrationProvenance.Policy: Semantic copy into GRACE 4 current state; legacy sources remain byte-for-byte as migration provenance.

Guidelines.ContentFirst: Editor mode, view, sidebar, live reload, clipboard, and extension operations never silently lose or rewrite document content.
Guidelines.ExplicitRisk: External links, shell paths, rich clipboard content, imports, and security-sensitive actions expose confirmation or a clear blocked state.
Guidelines.LocalTruth: File, watcher, save, diff, recent-document, and project states reflect persisted or observed local truth rather than optimistic UI assumptions.
Guidelines.AccessibleControls: Core editing, navigation, command palette, menu, update, and recovery controls remain keyboard-usable and visibly stateful.
Guidelines.PerformanceVisible: Startup, large-document, search, pending-open, and lazy-renderer behavior uses deterministic budgets and observable degradation.
Guidelines.CrossPlatformHonesty: macOS, Windows, and Linux capability differences are explicit; unsupported platform behavior fails closed without false success.
Guidelines.ExtensionIsolation: Extension-host or TokMo integration failure never corrupts the active document or bypasses the typed IPC and permission boundary.
Guidelines.ReleaseContinuity: Installed version, updater state, release metadata, and Homebrew availability remain understandable and consistent to the user.
Guidelines.LargeDocumentContract: Approved by the owner on 2026-10-29 from the C-LARGE-DOC-STAGE-0 decision gate (owner-decision.md in that change; budgets are acceptance gates for later waves, never regression excuses). Target sizes: 1 MB is the comfortable supported target; the 1.7 MB / 9,000+ section shape is the stress/reference shape that must remain usable; documents up to 100 KB are the ordinary baseline. Budgets: ordinary documents get first visible content within 400 ms and p95 input-to-next-paint within 50 ms with a +20 percent same-run relative tolerance against the recorded baseline; the 1 MB target gets open within 1,500 ms and typing p95 within 100 ms; the 1.7 MB stress shape gets open within 4,000 ms, typing p95 within 250 ms, longest main-thread task within 300 ms and scroll frame p95 within 50 ms. Chromium/Long-Tasks and WebKit/event-loop-lag-proxy are separate labelled series and are never merged. Wave order: Wave A (progressive mount) first, then B1/B2, B3 last; Wave B starts only after the Wave A baseline is re-shot on the same corpus. Crash durability: no-WAL honest contract — no unsaved-recovery guarantee is claimed, a hard crash may lose edits since the last committed save, the atomic old-or-new save is its own prerequisite change, and any WAL requires separate approval. Experimental access: any experimental large-document path ships local, default-off and session-latched behind a visible Experimental setting that never persists silently; default flips require separately approved changes. Wave A decisions (owner-approved 2026-11-02 from the C-LARGE-DOC-WAVE-A decision document): time-to-input within first-visible-content + 250 ms on every shape; tail-mount completion within 2500 ms at the 1 MB shape and 25000 ms at the stress shape (background work — the ceiling guards against never-finishing mounting, not speed); on the progressive path the contract's open budget is satisfied by time-to-input, with first visible content and tail-mount reported as separate phases, never summed; hard budgets are gated by the baseline artifacts and the owner-run acceptance capture while CI asserts numeric emission with loose non-flaky ceilings (the ratified R-6 reading); and two accepted narrowings — oversized single blocks mount as one unit (content-chunking stays a Wave B candidate with the recorded numbers), and opens restoring a remembered cursor or block cache stay on the legacy path until progressive open learns cursor restoration.
